q: What are our competitors spending on ads for the same products?
answer:
Short answer: we can't see competitors' ad spend in our data — the ad delivery views (paid_media / product_ads) only report our platforms' delivery (Meta & Google) and allocated spend to our products. There is no source here that holds competitor spend by product.

Why that's the case and what it means
- Platform privacy: Meta and Google do not share other advertisers' spend to our account; our paid_media shows only our impressions, clicks and spend.
- Catalogue limits: the product ad spend (allocated) and paid_media metrics are our delivered spend (order-date allocated or delivery date), not market or auction-level spend — there is no competitor metric in the catalogue.
- Practical impact: you cannot judge relative share or bidding pressure from these tables alone; scaling a product because it has high ROAS here may still face higher auction costs or competitor saturation.

Useful alternatives I can run or help you get
- Show where our unallocated product-ad spend is going (by campaign and ad_platform) — helps understand if large spend is hidden in broad campaigns. (Recommended next step.)
- Pull our platform auction signals: rising CPC/CPM or falling CTR by campaign or product (I can fetch ad spend, cpc, cpm, ctr by campaign/ad_platform over time) to infer rising competition on those product targets.
- Use external tools / platform UIs: request Google Auction Insights or Meta competitive metrics (share, overlap) from the ad accounts — those live tools are the direct source for competitor spend/share.

Worth checking: run an ad-platform breakdown of spend, CPC and CPM for the last 7 days and compare with the prior 7 days to spot rising auction costs.

Period: 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-28 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-28
